study.title: Mark 3 Jesus" authority, increasing opposition and the true family of God
study.overview: Mark 3 shows a clear advance between healing, conflict and revelation. Jesus heals on the Sabbath, which exposes the hardness of his opponents; then his fame draws multitudes, while unclean spirits and religious leaders react in opposite ways to his identity. Then he calls the twelve to be with him, preach and share in his ministry. The chapter ends with a decisive redefinition of kinship: the closest family to Jesus is made up of those who do the will of God. The text presents Christ as Lord of the Sabbath, the winner of evil, a disciple-former and the center of a new community.

outline.title: Healing on Saturday and hostility of leaders
outline.explanation: Jesus confronts the rigid interpretation of the Sabbath by healing a man with his atrophied hand. His question forces the choice between doing good and doing evil, but the opponents are silent and soon plan his death.

outline.title: Crowds, healings and testimony of the unclean spirits
outline.explanation: Jesus withdraws, but the crowd follows him from many places. He heals many and limits physical pressure upon himself, while the filthy spirits recognize his identity, although he rebuke them not to disclose it.

outline.title: The Choice of the Twelve Apostles
outline.explanation: On the mountain, Jesus calls them whom He wanted and set twelve to be with him, preach, and exercise authority over sickness and demons. The list of the twelve highlights that the group is composed of real and varied people, including Judas Iscariot, who would betray him.

outline.title: Accusations, Jesus" defense and the true family
outline.explanation: The pressure increases: family members think that he has lost his judgment, scribes accuse him of acting by the chief of the demons, and Jesus responds by showing the incoherence of this accusation. Then he declares that his closest family is not defined by blood, but by obeying God.

study.context: The chapter is organized around controversies, signs and teaching about discipleship. The notes indicate that the healing of the atrophied hand's man resumes the conflict with the Pharisees on the Sabbath. They also show that the disciples' call on the mount recalls the solemn form as God called servants in the Old Testament. As for the final passage, the notes observe that the relatives of Jesus do not believe in him at that moment, which helps to understand the tension between family ties and adherence to his call.
study.theology: Mark 3 emphasizes that Jesus" authority is moral, spiritual, and messianic. He does not treat the Sabbath as a pretext for omission of good; on the contrary, he reveals that doing good, saving and restoring is in harmony with the will of God. Religious opposition appears as spiritual blindness: leaders see a miracle and respond with hardness of heart and blasphemy. At the same time, unclean spirits recognize who Jesus is, but their recognition is not obedient faith. The choice of the twelve shows that the ministry of Jesus is communal and sent: to be with him comes before preaching and healing. Finally, the chapter redefines family as obedience to God, not natural privilege. A Protestant evangelical reading here sees repentance, faith and follow-up of Jesus as a concrete expression of God's will, without reducing discipleship to external ties.

scholarViews.insight: Jesus" question about doing good or doing evil on the Sabbath shames adversaries, but does not change their hearts.
Jesus calls the twelve to be with him and then send them to preach; the call begins in communion before the mission.
The atrophied hand is mentioned as a man with a mysad, and the note highlights that opponents have maliciously watched him.

questions: In what situations do I use religion to avoid the good God wants me to do?
My reaction to Jesus is of obedient faith, like those who do the will of God, or just of distant admiration?
Am I seeking to be with Jesus before I want to act in his name?
How does my life show that God's will defines my priorities more than human ties or external expectations?
study.practice: This week, choose a concrete act of mercy that you usually postpone for convenience, fear or religious formalism, and practice it intentionally. Then take daily time to be with Jesus in prayer and Bible reading before thinking of any ministerial task or important decision. It is also worth examining whether there is any area in which you are calling prudence what, in practice, is hardness of heart.
study.uncertainty: The given notes do not detail all the elements of the text, especially the contents of verses 7 to 12 and 20 to 30, so the synthesis of these passages depends mainly on the biblical chapter itself. Tyndale's note about Jesus" family in 3:21 states that the gospel does not explain whether motivation was sincere concern or hostility; therefore, this issue remains open. It is also not possible to safely affirm, from the notes, the exact identity of the hill or the mentioned house, nor expand beyond what the text and notes support.
